rationale: A wins because it keeps the launch inside the evidence. "Mercury Personal runs on partner banks, not a charter — what that means for your money" is a real structural angle with the right proof gates; B's "What the SVB windfall became" tries to make a causal SVB growth story out of facts it was not given. B has useful shapes, but "the bank startups fled to after SVB" is exactly the kind of overclaim a fintech reporter will spike on sight.
gaps_in_A: "same arrangement that has drawn scrutiny across consumer fintech" imports outside regulatory context the update did not supply. It may be true, but this exercise did not give it.
"Every kept angle currently leans on undisclosed numbers" is too blunt. The partner-bank angle mainly needs partner names, custody mechanics, and FDIC disclosure, not pricing or deposit targets.

"If you want a current news peg... run `newsjack-detector` first" sends the founder hunting for freshness when the launch is already the peg. The better next step is proof collection, not peg shopping.
gaps_in_B: "the bank startups fled to after SVB" overstates the supplied fact. The update says Mercury became well known as an alternative after SVB collapsed, not that startups fled to it.
"What the SVB windfall became: 200,000 businesses, a profit claim, and now a consumer bank" is the bad swing. No fact connects SVB to the 200,000 businesses, profitability, or consumer launch.

"the alternative that absorbed startup deposits" is invented causality dressed as context. B even admits it needs "how much of the 200,000-business base arrived after SVB," which means the kept angle should have been refused or heavily caveated.

"defensive-comment" gives the charter angle a crisis posture without a supplied regulatory event, enforcement action, or customer harm signal. That is how a useful banking-plumbing story becomes alarmist.
